Let the side of the cube be (s) cm. When the 800 g mass is on the cube the cube is just fully submerged, so the buoyant force equals the weight of the cube plus the mass:

[ho_{	ext{water}},s^{3} = ho_{	ext{cube}},s^{3} + 800]

After the mass is removed, 2 cm of the cube is above the water, so the submerged volume is (s^{3}-2s^{2}). The buoyant force then equals the weight of the cube alone:

[ho_{	ext{water}},(s^{3}-2s^{2}) = ho_{	ext{cube}},s^{3}]

Eliminating (ho_{	ext{cube}}) from the two equations gives (2s^{2}=800), hence (s^{2}=400) and (s=20) cm.  Thus the side length of the cube is 20 cm.
